text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabweans can now walk around without their national identity cards after the Supreme Court on Monday found it unconstitutional to compel people to carry their cards. The ruling effectively bans police from arresting those found without cards on their person.

- No solution appears in sight for troubled Air Zimbabwe whose operations have been crippled by striking pilots and flight engineers, with disgruntled crews and management accusing each other of spurning negotiations.

- Zimbabwe Newspapers made a profit of Z$73 million before tax last year, almost all of it from its six papers, with a post tax profit of Z$48 million. This was close to 2.75 times the profit recorded in 1995.

- Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa on Monday flew into Harare for talks with his Zimbabwean counterpart Robert Mugabe on the Zairean crisis ahead of a summit of leaders from the Great Lakes region, South Africa and Zimbabwe.
